title: Chicken Shawarma
subtitle: Levantine spiced marinated chicken
excerpt: Chicken thighs marinated in a blend of warm Levantine spices, then roasted or griddled until the edges are charred and the meat is juicy inside. Served carved into flatbreads with tahini, garlic sauce, pickles, and fresh vegetables.

recipe.sourceNotes: Shawarma is the Levantine version of a family of rotating-spit roast preparations found across the Middle East and Central Asia (döner kebab in Turkey, gyros in Greece). The name derives from the Turkish word çevirme, meaning turning. Shawarma uses chicken, lamb, or mixed meats heavily spiced with a blend that typically includes cumin, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, allspice, and often cardamom; the exact blend varies by country and by cook. At home without a vertical spit, the dish is most successfully made by marinating chicken thighs and roasting or griddling them at high heat to get charred edges. The chicken is then sliced thinly across the grain and served in flatbreads with garlic sauce (toum), tahini, pickled turnips, tomatoes, and cucumber.

content.text: Marinate the chicken overnight if possible; the spices penetrate more deeply. The chicken needs char at the edges to taste authentic; roast at a high temperature or finish under a very hot grill. Slice the rested chicken thinly across the grain before serving, not in chunks.
Mix the yoghurt, lemon juice, garlic, all spices, oil, and salt to form the marinade. Add the chicken thighs and turn to coat. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.

Heat the oven to 220°C / fan 200°C / gas 7. Arrange the chicken in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes until the edges are charred in places and the juices run clear. For extra char, grill under a very hot grill for 3 to 4 minutes at the end.
Rest for 5 minutes, then slice thinly across the grain. Serve in warm flatbreads with garlic sauce, tahini, tomato, cucumber, and pickled vegetables.
